sources.title: Local stability of ground states in locally gapped and weakly interacting quantum spin systems
sources.author: Joscha Henheik, Stefan Teufel, Tom Wessel
sources.section: Abstract and statement of the main theorem (the paper's own Theorem 3), read via WebFetch summary, not the full proof
sources.provenance: peer-reviewed journal article, open-access PMC copy
sources.claim: For a weakly interacting spin system with a uniform on-site gap g and finite interaction range R, a localized perturbation P supported in a region X changes the ground state's local expectations only by an amount decaying exponentially in the distance from X: tr((rho_P-rho)A) <= c1||A|| e^{-c2 dist(Y,X)}, with c1, c2 existential constants depending only on R and g, no numeric threshold given.
sources.relevance: This is the closest published match to the 'boundary-influence decay' shape the advisor's brief proposes (an LPPL/HTW-type local-stability bound), and a plausible target FORM for BA1's pre-registration; it is for quantum spin systems with bounded on-site terms only, not lattice gauge theories with unbounded Casimir on-site terms, and its constants are existential, which is exactly the gap this project's AM2/AV1 explicit-constant method is suited to close for this specific model, as it already did for Yarotsky's existential constants.
sources.unresolved: Whether the paper's proof technique (not read past the abstract/theorem statement) is adaptable to unbounded on-site terms and the coarse-factor SU(2) geometry used here, or whether an independent in-house argument (extending AV1's product-ordering split shell by shell) is the more direct route, is not determined by this reading.

sources.title: Cluster expansion for ground states of local Hamiltonians
sources.author: Alvise Bastianello, Spyros Sotiriadis
sources.version_date: submitted 2016-01-11; published Nuclear Physics B 909 (2016) p.1020
sources.provenance: peer-reviewed journal article (published version), preprint host
sources.claim: Develops a cluster-expansion technique for ground states of general local Hamiltonians, deriving functional equations for cluster amplitudes and diagrammatic rules, and extends the locality statements to unitary time evolution (equilibration, work statistics).
sources.relevance: A general precedent for treating a ground state as a cluster/polymer expansion (the same conceptual move this lens's own Round32 memo Section 5.1 sketched, unused in the admitted AV1 proof, which used the simpler product-ordering split instead); potentially informative for BA1 if the simpler split does not suffice, but not itself read at derivation depth and not lattice-gauge-specific.
sources.unresolved: No explicit numeric convergence radius, boundary-condition-independence statement, or finite-volume convergence rate was found in the abstract; the paper's actual constants and hypotheses were not read.

sources.title: Dynamics and equilibrium states of infinite systems of lattice bosons
sources.author: Andreas Deuchert, Jonas Lampart, Marius Lemm
sources.version_date: arXiv:2505.13170, v3 read (dated 2025-06 by the fetch)
sources.section: Abstract and stated main results, read via WebFetch summary of the PDF text
sources.provenance: preprint (arXiv), not confirmed peer-reviewed in this pass
sources.claim: Proves Lieb-Robinson bounds of the exponential form exp(-mu(|r|-v t)) for infinite systems of lattice bosons with unbounded interactions, under uniform bounds on moments of the local particle-number operator, extending prior finite-volume unbounded-interaction Lieb-Robinson results (including Nachtergaele-Sims-type work) to the infinite-volume dynamics.
sources.relevance: A 2025 candidate upgrade path for the dynamics sub-round (BB): if its hypotheses translate to this project's compact-manifold Casimir on-site operators, it would give an EXPONENTIAL rather than the polynomial F(r)=(1+r)^-4 decay Nachtergaele-Sims (already used by AQ1) supplies, which would sharpen any boundary-shell bound; not adopted as a premise here.
sources.unresolved: The WebFetch summary's claim that the paper 'demonstrates applicability to lattice gauge theories' and 'incorporat[es] unbounded interaction terms through careful moment estimates... relevant for gauge-theoretic Hamiltonians' reads as the summarizing model's own inference, not a quoted statement from the paper; this is NOT treated as established and is recorded as an open question, not a claim, pending an actual read of the paper's hypotheses (uniform bounds on moments of a LOCAL PARTICLE NUMBER operator) against this project's Casimir/holonomy on-site operators, which are not literally boson number operators. The primary route for BB1 remains the already-in-house Nachtergaele-Sims citation via AQ1; this paper is a lead only.

sources.title: Quantum Simulation of Gauge Theories for Particle and Nuclear Physics
sources.author: Zohreh Davoudi
sources.version_date: submitted 2026-05-19; Contribution to Proceedings of the 42nd International Symposium on Lattice Field Theory (LATTICE2025)
sources.claim: Surveys quantum-computational approaches to lattice field theory, framing quantum simulation as offering polynomially efficient algorithms where classical lattice methods (e.g. dense-matter sign problems) are limited.
sources.relevance: Direct evidence that quantum simulation of lattice gauge theories is an active, funded (DOE-supported per the earlier related search) research programme in 2025-2026, supporting the brief's 'patents or government programmes on quantum simulation of lattice gauge theories' search item; relevant background for the applications-stage discussion of what an SU(2) Kogut-Susskind result could mean for that programme, but named no specific SU(2)/SU(3) Hamiltonian formulation or funding agency in the portion read.
sources.unresolved: Whether the full paper discusses SU(2) or SU(3) specifically, Hamiltonian (Kogut-Susskind) formulations, or names a specific government program by number, was not determined from the abstract alone; not pursued further this loop given scope.
